intro: Make a PDF booklet rearranges and places the pages of a document so that, once printed double-sided and folded in half, you get a booklet that reads in order: a wedding programme, a club newsletter, a zine or an instruction manual. Each sheet holds two pages, one on each side of the fold.

Pick the paper: A4 for an A5 booklet, A3 for an A4 booklet or Letter for a half-letter booklet. Pages are scaled to fit their half of the sheet. If the page count is not a multiple of 4, blank pages are added; with “The last page stays the back cover”, ticked by default, the blanks go before the last page so the back cover stays at the back.

Right binding is for publications read from right to left. Under “More options” you can leave a gutter at the fold, in millimetres, so the spine does not swallow the text, and split a thick document into several signatures by setting how many sheets each one holds; they are then sewn or glued together.

The output can be a single PDF to print double-sided flipping on the short edge, or two PDFs for manual duplex: the fronts and the backs, the latter already in reverse order. When it is done you see a preview of the sheets and can flip through the booklet. Everything happens in your browser, with no upload.

faq.a: With the duplex PDF, choose double-sided flipping on the short edge and “Actual size” in the print dialog. Then fold the stack in half and staple it along the fold.
Choose the “Manual duplex” output. Print the fronts first, flip the stack without rotating it, put it back in the tray and print the backs.

faq.q: How many sheets should each signature have?
faq.a: It depends on the paper thickness: a signature with too many sheets folds badly and the middle pages stick out. With the value 0 everything goes into a single signature.
